title: Simulation of an embedded call phase
statement:
Let $S,H$ be state types, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, and let a source machine with $k$ work tapes and a host machine with $l$ work tapes both use the Boolean alphabet. Let $\iota$ inject the source tape indices into the host tape indices, and let $e:S	o H$ be an injective state map. Choose host states $e_0$ and $a_0$ with $e_0
e a_0$, and assume $e(q)
e a_0$ for every source state $q$. Let $q_e,q_x$ be source states. Suppose the host transition at $e_0$, for every input and work-tape reading, is the source transition from $q_e$ with its state renamed by $e$; and at each state $e(q)$ with $q
e q_x$, the host transition agrees in the same way with the source transition from $q$. For any host tape contents and head positions, any prefix output list, source configurations $c,d$ with $c$ in state $q_e$, and any $t>0$, if the source run avoids $q_x$ at every time strictly between $0$ and $t$ and reaches $d$ at time $t$, then the host run from the configuration formed by embedding $c$ into the host tapes, preserving the other host tapes and prefixing the output by the given list, with state set to $e_0$, reaches the correspondingly embedded configuration from $d$ with state renamed by $e$ at time $t$. The host run has no configuration in state $a_0$ at any time from $0$ through $t$.

S and H are state types
x is a Boolean input word
src is a k-work-tape Boolean-alphabet machine with states S

host transitions at enter agree for all input and work readings with the embedded source transition at entry
host transitions at embedded q agree for every q other than exit and all input and work readings
tapes, heads, and output prefix are arbitrary host tape data
c and d are source configurations on input x
the source run avoids exit at every time strictly between 0 and t
the source run reaches d at time t
